body_markdown:
Holiday hosting has a way of making every extra chair, spare bedroom, and flat surface suddenly look very important. The dining table needs to become a table again. The entryway’s collection of shoes, bags, and mystery mail starts looking less charming. And if overnight guests are on the way, the spare room has to stop being “the room where things go for now.”


A quick[hosting reset](https://www.publicstorage.com/blog/seasonal/how-to-prepare-your-home-to-host-a-holiday.html) can make a home feel ready for company without turning the two days before a gathering into a full-house overhaul. Start with the spaces guests will use, open up the areas where people will gather, and let the rest wait.


## Key Takeaways


- Start with the guest room, entryway, bathroom, dining area, and living room.
- Focus on open walkways, sleeping space, and surfaces guests will use.
- Use a temporary hosting bin for smaller everyday items that can wait until after the gathering.
- A short-term storage rental can create room for eligible furniture, boxes, and household items during the holiday season.
- Check current facility rules, availability, access details, and offer terms before reserving a unit.


## Choose the Spaces Guests Will Use


A full-home reset can wait. Start with the spaces that will do the most work while people are visiting.


**Guest Space** **Quick Hosting Goal**


Entryway Clean up the floor and leave room for coats and shoes


Living room Create comfortable seating and a spot for drinks or snacks


Dining area Give the table room for meals, games, or conversation


Guest room Make space for a bed, luggage, and a few personal items


Bathroom Tidy the counter and set out fresh towels


Kitchen Open enough counter space for cooking and serving


This isn’t about making your home look untouched. It’s about making it easy for guests to walk in, set down a bag, sit comfortably, and settle in.


## Get the Guest Room Ready First


A spare bedroom can slowly become home to boxes, extra furniture, holiday decor, and projects that are waiting for their moment. Then someone says they’re staying overnight, and the room’s original purpose becomes very obvious.


Start with the bed, floor, and one surface for a guest’s belongings. If boxes or furniture are taking up the room, decide whether they can go somewhere else in your home, or if you need to[keep them in a storage unit](https://www.publicstorage.com/blog/organizing/be-the-hostess-with-the-mostess-how-to-use-a-storage-unit-to-host-a-party.html) for a little while.


A welcoming guest room can be simple:


- Fresh sheets and a blanket
- Space for a bag or suitcase
- A small surface for a phone, book, or glass of water
- A lamp or easy-to-reach light
- A spot for a jacket or overnight clothes


## Tidy the Spaces Guests Will Notice First


A packed drawer can wait until January. The dining table covered in mail, the bathroom counter full of daily products, and the[entryway floor](https://www.publicstorage.com/blog/organizing/what-is-a-drop-zone-in-a-house-your-guide-to-getting-organized.html) full of shoes are harder to ignore during a gathering.


Start with the areas that affect how guests move through the home:


- Entryway floor
- Dining table
- Kitchen counters
- Coffee table
- Guest-room bed and floor
- Bathroom counter


A basket or lidded bin can gather smaller everyday items while you work. Keep it somewhere you’ll remember after the visit, rather than creating a mystery box that appears again next summer.


## Use Temporary Storage for Larger Household Items


Sometimes the hosting challenge isn’t loose clutter. It’s the extra chair, bulky boxes, unused furniture, or household overflow that has claimed the room you want guests to use.


A[short-term storage rental](https://www.publicstorage.com/blog/storage-tips/the-pros-of-month-to-month-storage-rentals.html) can offer breathing room for eligible clean, dry furniture, boxed household items, seasonal decor, and other belongings that don’t fit your plans for the next few weeks. This can be especially helpful when a guest room has become a storage room or a dining area has turned into a holding zone.


Before reserving, review current facility rules, item restrictions, availability, access details, and offer terms for your location.


## Make the Entryway Easier to Navigate


The entryway is the first part of your home guests see, and it can fill up quickly once coats, shoes, bags, and umbrellas arrive.


Clean up the floor and create one obvious landing spot for purses, coats, and shoes. A bench, basket, hooks, tray, or open corner can be plenty. If you have a coat closet, leave some hanging room instead of filling every inch with your own jackets.


The goal isn’t a perfectly styled entryway. It’s avoiding the moment when everyone has to step over shoes to say hello.


## Give the Dining Table Its Job Back


A dining table can quietly become a desk, craft station, package landing zone, and homework spot between meals. Before hosting, move those everyday items to their next place or gather them in a temporary bin.


Once the table is open, keep the setup easy. A tablecloth, runner, candles, or a bowl of fruit can make it feel ready without launching a decorating project at the last minute.


An open dining table can also become one of the most useful places in the house for a holiday gathering, whether it holds dinner, desserts, board games, or a buffet spread.


## The 48-Hour Holiday Hosting Plan


A two-day timeline keeps the work from piling up on the morning guests arrive. Start with the rooms that need the most attention, then save the small finishing touches for later.


**When** **Focus**


Two days before Get the guest room, dining table, and entryway ready.


One day before Relocate larger items, wash linens, and reset the bathroom.


Morning of Tidy visible surfaces, set out towels, and leave room for coats and bags.


Just before guests arrive Turn on a lamp, put out water or snacks, and stop cleaning.


That final step helps the whole plan come together. Guests came to spend time with you, not inspect whether the junk drawer is organized.


## FAQs About Holiday Hosting Prep


**How do I prepare my house for overnight holiday guests?**


Start with the guest room, bathroom, entryway, and dining area. Make space for sleeping, set out fresh linens and towels, and leave room for a guest’s bag and personal items.


**What should I declutter before guests arrive?**


Focus on visible, high-use areas, including the entryway, dining table, kitchen counters, living room, bathroom counter, and guest-room floor.


**Can storage help when preparing for holiday guests?**


A short-term storage rental can create room for eligible furniture, boxes, seasonal decor, and household items that don’t fit your hosting plans. Check current facility rules and availability before reserving.


**How can I make a small home feel more spacious for guests?**


Keep walkways open, reduce furniture crowding, open up the dining table, and give guests a place for coats, bags, and overnight items.


## Make Room for the People Coming Over


Holiday hosting doesn’t call for a picture-perfect home. It calls for room to gather, eat, sleep, and linger over one more story after dinner.


Get the spaces that matter most ready, let the rest wait, and enjoy the people who came to fill the house.
